s: The direction of heat flow between two body depends on which of the following?
x: Heat flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature, so the direction depends only on their temperatures.

s: Blowing air with open pipe is an example of
x: Blowing air through an open pipe keeps the gas at the constant atmospheric pressure, so it is an isobaric process.

s: A cycle tyre bursts suddenly. This represents an
x: A tyre bursts so suddenly that there is no time for heat exchange with the surroundings, so the expansion is adiabatic.

s: Iodine can be separated from a mixture of iodine and potassium chloride by
x: Iodine sublimes on heating while KCl does not, so sublimation separates them. Filtration and sedimentation only work for insoluble solids and distillation for liquids.

s:
Which of the following is an example of sublimation?

I. Dry ice

II. Camphor

III. Ice
x: Dry ice (solid CO2) and camphor change directly from solid to gas, so they sublime. Ice melts to liquid water, so it is not an example.

s: When oil floats on water, the surface tension of water
x: When oil spreads over water it forms a film that considerably lowers the surface tension of the water surface, so the surface tension decreases considerably.

s: Gaseous exchange takes place in leaves through tiny pores for the purpose of photosynthesis. What are these pores ?
x: Stomata are the tiny pores in leaves through which gases are exchanged. Chloroplast and chlorophyll are involved in photosynthesis, and the vacuole is a storage sac.

s: The ultimate cause of water movement in a plant stem against gravity is
x: Transpiration from leaves creates a suction (transpiration pull) that draws water up the xylem against gravity, so it is the ultimate cause.

s: When the short circuit condition occurs, the current in the circuit
x: In a short circuit the resistance becomes almost zero, so by Ohm's law the current rises very sharply.

s: A lemon kept in water in a glass tumbler appears to be larger than its actual size. It is because of
x: Light from the lemon bends (refracts) as it passes from water to air through the glass, so the lemon appears magnified.

s: The splitting of different colours of light in a prism is
x: Splitting of white light into its colours in a prism is dispersion, caused by different wavelengths refracting by different amounts.

s: A soap bubble shows colours when illuminated with white light. This is due to ……… .
x: Colours in a soap bubble come from interference of light reflected from the front and back surfaces of the thin film.

s: The pH of water at 25° C is 7. When it is heated to 100° C, the pH of water
o: decreases up to 50° C and then increases
x: On heating, water ionises more, so [H+] increases and pH falls below 7 (about 6.1 at 100°C), although the water stays neutral.

s: A fan produces a feeling of comfort during hot weather, because
o: our body radiates more heat in air.
x: A fan speeds up evaporation of perspiration, and evaporation takes heat from the body, so we feel cool. The fan does not supply cool air.

s: In which one of the following physiological processes, excess water escapes in the form of droplets from a plant ?
x: Guttation is the loss of excess water as liquid droplets from leaf margins. Transpiration loses water as vapour.

s: In negative acceleration, the velocity of a body ............ .
x: Negative acceleration (retardation) means velocity decreases with time.

s: Whether an object will float or sink in a liquid, depends on
o: mass of the object and density of liquid only.
difference in the densities of the object and liquid.
mass and shape of the object only.
x: Floating or sinking depends on whether the object's density is less or more than the liquid's, i.e. on the difference in densities, not on mass or shape alone.

s: Of the two bulbs,one glows brighter than the other. Which bulb has a higher resistance?
Which of the following devices can be used to detect radiant heat?
x: A thermopile is made of thermocouples and detects radiant heat by the voltage generated when radiation heats its junctions.

s: Why do water droplets always take a round shape when dropped onto plane surfaces?
o: Due to the presence of Eddy current in the air
Due to exertion of surface tension by the molecules
x: Surface tension pulls the surface molecules inward, which minimises surface area, so a droplet takes a round shape.

s: Thermal capacity of a body depends on the
o: mass and shape of the body only.
mass, shape and temperature of the body.
x: Thermal capacity (C = m·s) depends on the body's mass (and material), not on its shape or temperature, so of the listed options only 'mass of the body only' fits.

s: We feel cool when we sit near the fan, this is because
o: air vapourises the sweat on our body.
we feel cool when air touches the body.
x: Moving air from the fan evaporates sweat, and evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, causing the cooling feeling. The fan does not cool the air.

s: Curie point is the temperature at which
x: The Curie point is the temperature above which a ferromagnetic metal loses its magnetic properties and becomes paramagnetic.

s: A ball balanced on a vertical rod is an example of
x: A ball balanced on top of a vertical rod is in unstable equilibrium: a small displacement lowers its potential energy, so it moves further away from its position instead of returning.

s: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a circular path. As it was revolving, the rope suddenly snaps. Then
x: When the string snaps, the centripetal force vanishes, so by Newton's first law the stone continues in the direction of its velocity at that instant, which is tangential to the circle.

s: Which type of plants are very tall and have hard and thick brown stem?
x: Trees are very tall plants with a hard, thick, brown woody stem (trunk). Herbs have soft green stems and shrubs are shorter and bushy.

s: Which is a natural colloid?
Specific gravity is defined as the ratio of
o: density of the substance to the density of water.
density of the substance to the density of water at 0°C.
density of water at 4°C to the density of the substance.
density of the substance to the density of water at 4°C.
x: Specific gravity (relative density) is the density of a substance divided by the density of water at 4°C, where water's density is maximum (1 g/cm³).

s: A glass vessel is filled with water up to the brim and a lid is fixed to it tightly. Then it is kept inside a freezer for hours. What is expected to happen?
o: The water freezes to ice and the level of ice comes down.
The water in the glass vessel freezes to ice.
The glass vessel breaks due to expansion as water freezes to ice.
The water does not freeze at all.
x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing. In a tightly sealed, full glass vessel it cannot expand, so the pressure breaks the vessel.

s: Glycol is added to aviation gasoline because it
x: Glycol (ethylene glycol type) is an anti-freeze additive. It lowers the freezing point of aviation fuel at high altitude, so the petrol does not freeze.

s: Which one of the following salts when dissolved in water makes the solution basic?
x: Sodium acetate is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (acetic acid). Its acetate ion hydrolyses to give OH-, so the solution is basic. NaCl is neutral; CuSO4 and FeCl3 are acidic.

s: Which chemical was an important symbol in our struggle for freedom?
x: Salt (sodium chloride) was the symbol of the freedom struggle through Gandhi's Dandi March and Salt Satyagraha (1930) against the salt tax.

s: Which one of the following is used as a mordant in dyeing and tanning industry?
x: Magnesium sulphate is used as a mordant in the dyeing and tanning industry. The other magnesium compounds are not used for this purpose.

s: Suppose you have four test tubes labelled as ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’ and ‘D’. ‘A’ contains plain water, ‘B’ contains solution of an alkali, ‘C’ contains solution of an acid, and ‘D’ contains solution of sodium chloride. Which one of these solutions will turn phenolphthalein solution pink?
x: Phenolphthalein turns pink in basic (alkaline) solution. Tube B has an alkali, while water, acid and NaCl solution are neutral or acidic and leave it colourless.

s: Which one among the following is not a property of salt?
o: Salts have ordered packing arrangements called lattices.
Salts have low melting points but high boiling points.
Salts conduct electricity when dissolved in water or even in the molten state.
x: Salts are ionic compounds with strong ionic bonds, so they have high melting and high boiling points. The statement that they have low melting points is false.

s: ………… is one of the most important technique for the separation of a mixture by passing it in solution or suspension through a medium in which the components move at different rates.
x: Chromatography separates mixture components because they move at different rates through a medium (stationary phase) carried by a solvent. Filtration, distillation and evaporation do not work this way.

s: What is the distance between a crest and a consecutive trough in a transverse wave?
x: The wavelength is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs. A crest and the adjacent trough are half a wavelength apart.

s: Which one of the following is not true for an electromagnetic wave?
o: Electromagnetic wave transports energy and momentum.
Electromagnetic wave can be polarised and reflected.
Electromagnetic wave propagation is described by the varying electric and magnetic fields.
x: Electromagnetic waves are transverse, with electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel. So the claim that they are longitudinal is not true.

s: The unit of the force constant k of a spring is
x: From Hooke's law F = kx, k = F/x, so its unit is newton per metre (N/m).

s: A conducting wire is dropped along East-West direction, then
o: induced current flows from West to East.
induced current flows from East to West.

s: Who propounded the theory of evolution?
x: Charles Darwin propounded the theory of evolution by natural selection (On the Origin of Species, 1859). Wallace independently proposed a similar idea, but Darwin is credited.

s: If an object moves with constant velocity, then which one of the following statement is not correct?
o: Its motion is along a straight line.
Its displacement increases linearly with time.
x: Constant velocity means constant speed and direction, so motion is in a straight line, acceleration is zero and displacement grows linearly. Speed changing with time is therefore not correct.

s: Which one of the following is a true fish as per the biological system of classification ?
x: The flying fish is a true fish (class Pisces) with gills and fins. Silverfish is an insect, jellyfish is a cnidarian and cuttlefish is a mollusc.

s: The refractive index of fused quartz is 1.46 and that of sapphire is 1.77. If vq is the speed of light in quartz and vs is the speed of light in sapphire, then which one of the following relations is correct?
x: Speed of light in a medium is v = c/n. Quartz has the lower refractive index (1.46 vs 1.77), so light travels faster in quartz: vq > vs.

s: What is the basis of classifying various plant tissues as meristematic tissue and permanent tissue?
x: Meristematic tissues are classified as such because their cells keep dividing, while permanent tissues have lost the capacity to divide. So the basis of classification is dividing capacity.

s: Which one of the following has a bilateral symmetry in its body organisation ?
x: Nereis (an annelid) is bilaterally symmetrical. Asterias and Echinus are echinoderms with radial symmetry as adults, and sea anemone is radially symmetrical.

s: Adamsia (sea anemone), Pennatula (sea pen), etc are examples of which Phylum?
x: Sea anemones (Adamsia) and sea pens (Pennatula) are cnidarians, formerly called Coelenterata, with a hollow gut cavity and tentacles.

s: Surface water of a lake is about to freeze. What will be the temperature (in °C) of water at the bottom of the lake?
x: Water is densest at 4 °C, so the densest water sinks to the bottom. The bottom stays at about 4 °C while ice forms at 0 °C on the surface.

s: A body is floating in a liquid partly immersed. The body and the liquid are taken to moon. The body
o: will continue to float as before.
x: Floating depends on the densities of the body and the liquid, not on g. The weight and the buoyant force both scale with g, so on the moon the body floats as before.

s:
Assertion (A) Asexual reproduction required only female animals.
Reason (R) Male animals are not capable for asexual reproduction.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
x: Asexual reproduction does not need gametes, and it can occur in either sex, e.g. budding and fragmentation. Both the assertion and the reason are false.

s: Which one among the following produces seeds but not flowers ?
x: Pine is a gymnosperm and bears naked seeds in cones without flowers. Cashew, coffee and groundnut are angiosperms that flower.

s: In which of the following animals hooves are not found ?
x: Hooves are found in ungulates such as deer, zebra and horse. The jackal is a carnivore with claws and paws, so it has no hooves.

s: Who was written book named ‘Origin of Species’?
x: Charles Darwin wrote 'On the Origin of Species' (1859), presenting natural selection.

s: Which of the following is the smallest bird in the world ?
x: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird in the world, about 5-6 cm long.

s: Which of the following compounds is used as drying agent?
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Non-metal oxides such as CO2 and SO2 are acidic, forming acids with water. Metal oxides are generally basic.

s: Which one among the following contains the most neutrons?
x: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number. Fe-59: 33; Cu-61: 32; Zn-61: 31; Zn-60: 30. So Fe-59 has the most.

s: Which of the following cannot be beaten into Sheets?
x: Gold, silver and aluminium are malleable and can be beaten into sheets. Potassium is a soft, reactive alkali metal that is not beaten into sheets.

s: At low temperature, lead behaves as a
x: Lead becomes a superconductor at very low temperature, about 7.2 K.

s: Which one of the following is an oxidation-reduction reaction?
x: In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, Mg is oxidised and O2 is reduced, so it is a redox reaction. The other options are neutralisation, combination and double displacement with no change in oxidation state.

s: Nitric acid does not react with
x: Gold is a noble metal that dissolves only in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), so nitric acid alone does not react with it. Copper, zinc and iron react.

s: The manufacturing of iron from iron ore involves the process of
x: Iron is extracted by reducing its oxide ore with coke, which acts as the reducing agent. So the process is reduction.

s: Bronze is an alloy of
x: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Brass is copper and zinc.

s: Maxwell is the unit of which one of the following?
x: The maxwell is the CGS unit of magnetic flux (1 Mx = 10^-8 Wb).

s: Which of the following has the lowest melting point ?
x: Tin melts at about 232 °C, lower than lead (327 °C), zinc (420 °C) and silver (962 °C).

s: What is the chemical formula for Sodium Chloride (Salt)?
x: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl: one Na+ ion combined with one Cl- ion, so the formula has no subscripts.

s: An amalgam of metal has which other element?
x: An amalgam is an alloy of a metal with mercury (Hg), the only common liquid metal.

s: Which of the following metals is the most reactive metal?
x: In the reactivity series calcium lies far above zinc, iron and copper, so it is the most reactive of these.

s: Which of the following metal is the heaviest?
x: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring metal, denser than iron, silver and nickel.

s: Which one among the following metals is used in fireworks to make a brilliant white light?
x: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, so it is used in fireworks for brilliant white light. Sodium gives yellow.

s: Zinc is used to protect iron form corrosion because zinc is
o: a good conductor of heat and electricity.
x: Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron, so it corrodes in preference to iron and protects it (galvanisation, sacrificial protection).

s: Which is used in storage batteries?
x: Lead (lead-acid accumulators) is used in storage batteries, with lead plates in sulphuric acid.

s: Which among the following elements comes under metalloids?
x: Germanium is a metalloid (semiconductor) while zinc, silver and gold are true metals.

s: The solution of which one of the following will have pH less than 7?
x: FeCl3 is a salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a weak base Fe(OH)3, so it hydrolyses to give an acidic solution (pH<7). NaCl and KCl are neutral and NaOH is basic.

s: A copper substances when exposed to air gains a green coating due to the formation of
Which one of the following is a non-dimensional quantity?
x: Strain is a ratio of change in length to original length, so it has no dimensions. The other quantities have dimensions.

s: The blackboard seems black because it
x: A blackboard appears black because it absorbs all colours and reflects none. Black is the absence of reflected light.

s: In the absence of the earth’s atmosphere, sky would appear
Which of the following is not a characteristics of a solid?
x: Solids have negligible compressibility because their particles are tightly packed, so high compressibility is not a characteristic of solids.

s: Smallest flowering plant is
x: Wolffia (duckweed) is the smallest flowering plant known.

s: Only male frog produce croacking sound because
o: female frog larynx but no vocal cord.
male frog have three pair of vocal cord.
male frog can magnify their voice with the help of sound box.
x: Male frogs have vocal sacs that act as resonating sound boxes that amplify the croak. Females lack these, though they do have a larynx.

s: A car undergoes a uniform circular motion. The acceleration of the car is
x: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the velocity direction keeps changing, so there is a centripetal acceleration of constant magnitude but changing direction. Hence it is non-zero and not constant as a vector.

s: A wheel-barrow is an example of
x: In a wheelbarrow the load lies between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort, which is a class II lever.

s: An example of modified underground stem is
Steel is more elastic than rubber because it
x: Elasticity is the ability to resist deformation and regain shape. Steel needs a larger deforming force for the same strain (higher Young's modulus) than rubber, so it is more elastic.

s: Mangifera indica is the scientific name of
x: Mangifera indica is the binomial name of the mango; guava, amla and jackfruit have different scientific names.

s: In the names Mangifera Indica (mango), Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion). The terms Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera represent the higher level of
x: The genus names Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera are taxa, i.e. units of classification; the specific epithet is the second word (indica, tuberosum, leo).

s: Which one of the following denotes a ‘true’ fruit?
o: When only the thalamus of the flower grows and develops into a fruit.
When only the receptacle of the flower develops into a fruit.
When fruit originates only from the calyx of a flower.
When only the ovary of the flower grows into a fruit.
x: A true fruit develops only from the ovary of the flower; fruits that develop from other parts such as the thalamus or receptacle are false fruits.

s: The threshold frequency of material is
o: the minimum frequency of light which can emit photoelectrons from materials.
the maximum frequency of light which can emit photoelectrons from materials.
The minimum energy required for the emission of photoelectron from a material.
x: Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of incident light that can eject photoelectrons from a material. Option 3 describes the work function (an energy), not the frequency.

s: A substance acquired in the form of brownish film on a piece of iron left in the open for some time is
x: Iron exposed to air and moisture forms a brownish layer of hydrated iron oxide, called rust.

s: In prokaryotic organisms, nuclear region is not surrounded by a membrane. This undefined nuclear region is known as
x: In prokaryotes the nuclear region without a membrane is the nucleoid. The nucleolus and nucleosome are structures in eukaryotic nuclei.

s: Which one among the following hormones stimulates the plant cells to grow in a manner such that the plant are to be bent towards light ?
x: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and promotes cell elongation there, so the plant bends towards light (phototropism).

s: Sycon (Scypha), Spongilla (Fresh water sponge) and Euspongia (Bath sponge) are example of which Phylum?
x: Sycon, Spongilla and Euspongia are sponges, which belong to Phylum Porifera.

s: Thermal conductivity of aluminium, copper and stainless steel increases in the order
x: Copper is the best conductor of heat, aluminium is next, and stainless steel is a poor conductor. So the order is stainless steel < aluminium < copper.

s: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
x: Silk is a natural protein fibre from silkworms. Rayon is semi-synthetic, and nylon and polyester are synthetic.

s: The number of angular and radial nodes for 4d orbital is respectively
x: For 4d, n=4 and l=2. Angular nodes = l = 2, and radial nodes = n-l-1 = 1.

s: Fabric made from ………does not get wrinkled easily.
x: Polyester is a synthetic fibre that resists wrinkling. Cotton, flax and silk crease easily.

s: If the xylem of a plant is mechanically blocked, which of the following functions of the plant will be affected?
x: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals (solutes) upward, so blocking it affects the transport of both.

s: Which of the following are amongst the few carbon-containing compounds not classified as organic?
x: Cyanides, along with oxides of carbon, carbonates and carbides, are carbon compounds traditionally treated as inorganic. Methane, propane and nucleic acids are organic.

s: Very small insoluble particles in a liquid may be separated it by using
x: Centrifugation spins the liquid so that very fine insoluble particles settle out. Decantation works only for larger particles that settle on their own.

s: Which one of the following statement about gravitational force is not correct?
o: It is experienced by all bodies in the universe.
It is a dominant force between celestial bodies.
It is a negligible force for atoms.
It is same for all pairs of bodies in our universe.
x: Gravitational force depends on the masses and the distance between the bodies (F = Gm1m2/r²), so it differs for different pairs of bodies.

s: The scientific name of peacock is
x: The Indian peafowl (peacock) is Pavo cristatus. The other names refer to other birds.

s: Which one of the following statements about bar magnet is correct?
o: The pole strength of the North pole of a bar magnet is larger than that of the South pole.
When a piece of bar magnet is bisected perpendicular to its axis, the North and South poles get separated.
When a piece of bar magnet is bisected perpendicular to its axis, two new bar magnets are formed.
The poles of a bar magnet are unequal in magnitude and opposite in nature.
x: Cutting a bar magnet perpendicular to its axis gives two smaller complete magnets, each with its own N and S poles. Poles cannot be isolated, and the two poles have equal strength.

s: What is formed when Magnesium is burnt?
x: Magnesium burns in air to form magnesium oxide, a white ash. It does not form baking soda, calcium carbonate or vinegar.

s: From which part of pant the ‘Asafoetida or heeng’ is obtained?
x: Asafoetida (heeng) is the dried latex (oleo-gum resin) exuded from the roots of Ferula plants.

s: Which one of the following is not a component of conducting tissue in plants?
x: Pericycle is a layer of cells just inside the endodermis and is not a conducting element; xylem (tracheids, fibres) and phloem (sieve tubes) are the conducting tissues.

s: Which one of the following gives the highest amount of hydrogen ions (H+)?
x: Gastric juice contains HCl (pH ~1.5-3.5), so it is the most acidic and has the highest H+ concentration; lemon juice is a weaker acid and the others are basic.

s: Which of the following acids is present in ant bites?
x: Ant bites inject formic acid (methanoic acid), as the notes state.

s: What is the name of a group of similar cells performing a specific function?
x: A group of similar cells performing a specific function is called a tissue; organs are made of several tissues.

s: Genes are made up of
x: Genes are segments of DNA, which is a nucleic acid.

s: When you walk on a woolen carpet and bring your finger near the metallic handle of a door, an electric shock is produced. This is because
o: charge is transferred from your body to the handle.
a chemical reaction occurs when you touch the handle.
the temperature of the human body is higher than that of the handle.
the human body and the handle arrive at thermal equilibrium by the process.
x: Walking on a carpet builds up static charge on the body by friction; touching the metal handle discharges it, so charge is transferred from the body to the handle.

s: If electric resistance is to be decreased, then the number of resistances should be connected in … .
x: In parallel, the reciprocals of resistances add, so the equivalent resistance is lower than the smallest resistance; series increases it.

s: The …… is connected in parallel in an electric circuit.
x: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component; fuse and ammeter are in series.

s: In the reaction between hydrogen sulphate ion and water HSO4− + H2O → H3O+ + SO42−, the water acts as
x: Water accepts a proton from HSO4- to form H3O+, so water acts as a Bronsted-Lowry base.

s: What is the shape of the two guard cells which enclose stomata ?
x: Guard cells enclosing a stoma are kidney (bean) shaped in dicots.

s: Which one of the following is a plant hormone ?
x: Cytokinin is a plant hormone promoting cell division; insulin, thyroxine and estrogen are animal hormones.

s: The SI unit of luminous emittance is
x: Luminous emittance (luminous flux per unit area) has SI unit lux (lumen per square metre); candela is luminous intensity and lumen is flux.

s: Which one of the following wave does not belong to the category of the other three?
x: X-rays, microwaves and radio waves are electromagnetic waves; sound waves are mechanical and need a medium.

s: The loudness of sound depends upon the
o: velocity of sound waves in the medium.
frequency and velocity of the sound waves.
x: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the sound wave (pitch depends on frequency).

s: Sound of frequencies below 20 Hz are called ……… .
x: Sound below 20 Hz is infrasound.

s: Bats detect obstacles in their path by receiving the reflected
x: Bats use ultrasound, receiving reflected ultrasonic waves to detect obstacles.

s: Which of following property of a proton cannot change while it moves freely in magnetic field?
x: Magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity so it does no work; speed and kinetic energy stay constant, while direction (velocity and momentum) changes.

s: Flemings “Left hand Rule” is associated with the effect of
x: Fleming's left hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, i.e. the effect of magnetic field on current.

s: What is the net force experienced by a bar magnet placed in a uniform magnetic field?
o: Depends upon length of the magnet
x: In a uniform field the forces on the two poles are equal and opposite, so net force is zero (only a torque acts).

s: Which one among the following waves carries the maximum energy per photon?
x: Photon energy E=hf is proportional to frequency; X-rays have the highest frequency among the options.

s: Which of the following represents a relation for heat lost = heat gained?
x: Heat lost by the hot body equals heat gained by the cold body is the principle of calorimetry; thermal equilibrium only means equal temperatures.

s: Which of the following has the lowest electrical resistivity?
x: Silver has the lowest resistivity of all metals, lower than aluminium, while nickel and nichrome (a heater alloy) have high resistivity.

s: A Galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting with it a
x: A galvanometer becomes a voltmeter when a high resistance is connected in series, so most of the voltage drops across the resistance and little current flows through the galvanometer.

s: The phenomena of electromagnetic induction is ……… .
o: the process of charging a body
the process of generating magnetic field due to a current passing through a coil
induced current in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil
the process of rotating a coil of an coil electric motor
x: Electromagnetic induction is the production of an induced current/emf in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil (change in magnetic flux).

s: Which one of the following metal is used in the filaments of photoelectric cells that converts light energy into electric energy?
x: Photoelectric cells use alkali metals with low work function, such as rubidium or caesium, which emit electrons easily when light falls on them; tungsten is used for bulb filaments.

s: Which one of the following could be the melting point of iron ?
x: Iron is a solid with a high melting point of about 1538°C, so 1500°C is the only option close to it.

s: A combustible gas is liberated when caustic soda solution is heated with
x: Zinc reacts with hot NaOH to give sodium zincate and hydrogen gas, which is combustible. NH4Cl would give ammonia, which is not combustible.

s: The only living tissue in plant xylem is
x: Xylem parenchyma is the only living cell type in xylem; tracheids, vessels (trachea) and fibres are dead at maturity.

s: Which of the following is not a connective tissue?
x: Cardiac muscle is a muscular tissue. Adipose, bone and areolar tissues are connective tissues.

s: Net movement of water from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane is called
The movement of water molecules through the plasma membrane is called
If cells are kept in some solution and the net result is that the cell swells up, then the solution is ………
x: In a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration outside), water enters the cell by osmosis and the cell swells; in a hypertonic solution it shrinks.

s: Which hormone is found in the gaseous form ?
x: Ethylene is the only plant hormone that is a gas (fruit ripening); abscisic acid, gibberellins and auxins are not gaseous.

s: A substance which is more than 80% in the cell is
x: Water is the most abundant component of the cell, making up more than 80% of it; protein, fat and minerals form much smaller fractions.

s: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
x: Electrostatic potential has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Velocity, force and angular momentum are vectors.

s: Identify the unit of measuring intensity of sound
What is the unit of the physical quantity, Momentum?
x: Momentum = mass × velocity, with unit kg m/s, which equals newton second (N·s), since 1 N = 1 kg m/s².

s: Which one of the following physical quantities has the same unit as that of pressure?
x: Stress is force per unit area, so it has the same unit as pressure (pascal, N/m²). Strain is dimensionless.

s: The resistivity of a material may be expressed in unit of
Which one of the following is not the unit of energy?
x: Joule, watt-hour and newton-metre are all units of energy. Kg·m/s² is the unit of force (newton), so it is not an energy unit.

s: The unit of momentum is
x: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹. The notes do not state this unit.

s: Which one of the following is the unit of Force?
x: The newton is the SI unit of force. The other options are units of pressure (pascal), power (watt) and energy (joule).

s: The symbol of SI unit of inductance is H. It stands for
x: The henry (H) is the SI unit of inductance.

s: The SI unit for electrical resistivity is
x: Resistivity ρ = RA/l has the unit ohm-metre.

s: Newton-metre (Nm) is the SI unit of which of the following physical quantity?
x: Torque = force × perpendicular distance, so its unit is N m. Force is in N, power in W and acceleration in m/s².
